purpose: Exercise an effects-disabled municipal information/service journey and preserve distinctions among community reports, provider claims, official source claims, cross-utility hypotheses, conflicting guidance, and independently verified resolution. The v0.5.0 corpus adds three synthetic Johannesburg City project-announcement controls for water-depot close-out, traffic-signal accessibility, and clinic reopening; project announcements must not be promoted into live operational status or verified outcomes.

need.description: Synthetic scenario testing water-outage guidance when official sources conflict.

route.notes: The official Contact Us page publishes fault@jwater.co.za for water-related incidents and +27 (0)10 061 4470 for logging calls/queries. This is a candidate contact pathway, not an action or universal routing rule. The /emergencies/ page also displays a different logging-call email and phone in its top section, with further numbers in its footer. Preserve each channel with its stated purpose; the 12-hour versus 24-hour target remains unresolved.

evidence.claim_scope: The URL labelled /emergencies/ renders a Daily water Notices heading, lists a 12-hour water-outage turnaround, and its top Logging calls section lists customerserviceemails@jwater.co.za and +27 (0)11 375 5555.
evidence.limitations: The same page footer separately lists fault@jwater.co.za for water-related incidents and other contact-centre numbers. The page bytes were not cryptographically hashed; preserve each section and stated purpose instead of collapsing channels.

evidence.claim_scope: The Daily Water Notices page lists a 24-hour water-outage turnaround and shows fault@jwater.co.za with +27 (0)10 061 4470 in its logging section.
evidence.limitations: The page footer repeats fault@jwater.co.za as water-incident-only and lists other contact-centre numbers. The content may distinguish purposes; do not assume every listed channel is interchangeable.

evidence.claim_scope: The official Contact Us page lists fault@jwater.co.za for logging water-related incidents only and +27 (0)10 061 4470 for logging calls/queries; it separately lists sms@jwater.co.za for interruption notifications.
evidence.limitations: Contact details were captured from the page at retrieved_at. This does not mean this reference case submitted a service request, prove a route is applicable in every situation, or resolve the turnaround-target conflict.

outcome.summary: Conflicting official service guidance requires human review before any exact target or submission route is presented as definitive.

permitted_claims: The checked official pages disagree on a stated water-outage turnaround target.

need.description: Synthetic question asking whether a dated public statement proves that a particular water interruption was caused by a power trip and whether supply is restored now.

route.notes: No case-specific routing or current status has been established by the synthetic public-statement fixture.

evidence.claim_scope: The South African Government's 10 September 2026 statement describes a multi-stakeholder meeting to address water-supply disruptions associated with intermittent power trips. This fixture records a synthetic summary of the statement topic; the page was not captured as evidence for this case.
evidence.limitations: Synthetic fixture only: no source retrieval timestamps or source-content digest are present. The statement is cross-utility context, not evidence that a specific resident's interruption was caused by electricity, not live outage/restoration status, and not proof of an intervention outcome.

outcome.summary: No incident-specific causal evidence or current restoration observation is included.

permitted_claims: The synthetic fixture describes the topic of a dated public statement about cross-utility coordination.
prohibited_inferences: The resident's specific interruption was caused by a power trip based only on this statement.
Water supply is restored now based on the historical statement.
The statement proves live outage status, completed repair, or measured intervention effect.
All Johannesburg water outages are caused by electricity interruptions.
The fixture timestamp or null digest is actual source-retrieval evidence.
